problem: About 9 percent of English tweets reached the limit, which frustrated users.
title: Twitter doubles its character limit from 140 to 280
context: Many English-language tweets hit the 140 character limit and users struggled to fit their thoughts.
decision_made: Raise the limit to 280 characters after a trial.
action_taken: Ran a trial with a subset of users, then rolled out in November 2017.
observed_outcome: In the trial only 5 percent of tweets were longer than 140 characters and about 1 percent hit the new limit, so timelines did not fill with long tweets.
lessons: A looser constraint relieved frustration without changing the feel of the product much.
limitations: Figures come mainly from Twitter itself. Academic work found that 280 characters still shapes how people write, and long-term effects on engagement were not checked here.

claims.claim_text: Twitter doubled its character limit to 280 after a trial.
Only about 1 percent of tweets hit the 280 limit, and about 12 percent were longer than 140.
